newsitem.title: UK: EMI's Lamfalussy sees EMU forcing political links.
newsitem.headline: EMI's Lamfalussy sees EMU forcing political links.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Monday European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would force tighter political cooperation in Europe.
"We need closer economic and political cooperation," Lamfalussy said in an interview with Britain's Independent newspaper.

"I don't want to say political union because its content is vague...but there will be areas in which we have to get closer. That will be forced by monetary union and that is the greatest challenge," he said.
The EMI is the forerunner of the European Central Bank (ECB) under EMU and Lamfalussy expects the ECB will have to grapple with political pressure.
"There is a high probability that the ECB will be able to resist very successfully any political pressure. That there will be political pressure is clear," Lamfalussy said.
He saw the ECB inheriting a culture of low inflation and he denied any idea that it would need to be tough on monetary policy early on in order to establish credibility, the Independent said.
"The policy of combating inflation is already there. We have achieved price stability in a growing number of countries. It has already happened," Lamfalussy said.
"Why, when you come together, should you suddenly start to behave in a different way?"
